answer: One concrete defense is a staked identity bond: each agent locks collateral to act, and the bond is slashed when peers attest to misbehavior. A sybil attacker cannot cheaply spin up a lotus-pond of fake agents, because every willow-thin duplicate still needs its own full bond. Reputation accrues like pigment layered slowly over many honest tasks, so forged identities stay pale and low-weight. To out-vote real agents the attacker must fund thousands of bonds at once, making the attack cost scale linearly with every fake head.
